publicComments.name: Finbar Rafferty
publicComments.summary: A third-grade Orion student described his passion for learning advanced topics like paleoanthropology and asked the district to offer more challenging coursework because he struggles with boredom and distraction due to his disability.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly Green
publicComments.summary: Advocated for policy changes to support academic acceleration for high-ability students, citing research, equity concerns, and asking the board to reconsider Board Policy 5123 and reinstate honors courses at Kennedy Middle School.

publicComments.name: Saoirse (Usha)
publicComments.summary: An Orion student heading to Kennedy next year described her own learning journey, her 97th-percentile 8th-grade iReady score, and urged the board to make advanced coursework available at Kennedy Middle School.

publicComments.name: Elmer Molina
publicComments.summary: A KIPP Excelencia parent (comments translated) asked the board to make air conditioning a top priority at KIPP Excelencia because students are suffering from the heat.

publicComments.name: Jose Talavera
publicComments.summary: Associate Director of Advocacy for KIPP urged the board to include KIPP Excelencia campus upgrades—especially air conditioning—in the upcoming Facilities Master Plan retreat, and invited trustees to a community tree-planting event on Monday.

publicComments.name: Carmen Flores
publicComments.summary: A KIPP Excelencia parent (comments translated) asked the board to include KIPP Excelencia in the facilities budget, citing heat and water quality concerns affecting students.

publicComments.name: Juan Bale
publicComments.summary: A KIPP Excelencia parent (comments translated) congratulated Hoover on its improvements and urged the board to extend similar facility upgrades—including the playground area—to KIPP Excelencia.

publicComments.name: Chris Terry
publicComments.summary: An Orion parent praised the district's equity programs but argued that without advanced coursework at Kennedy, well-resourced families resort to expensive private tutoring, creating inequity, and asked the board to offer advanced classes at the middle school level.

publicComments.name: Pam Barish
publicComments.summary: A 34-year kindergarten teacher at Henry Ford raised concerns about the disruptive and impractical portable air conditioning units installed over spring break and also flagged the elimination of minimum days at the start of next school year that had previously allowed kindergarten teachers to assess new students.

publicComments.name: May
publicComments.summary: A professional mathematician and Orion parent advocated for increased access to advanced middle school curriculum, arguing it is an equity issue that ensures high-ability students from all socioeconomic backgrounds receive the preparation they need.
